result.title: Hierarchy-GBP: Accelerating Factor Graph Inference via Abstraction and Recovery
result.summary: Gaussian Belief Propagation (GBP) is a distributed inference algorithm that passes messages in graphical models, making it attractive for scalable spatial intelligence. However, we find GBP most effective locally: it rapidly smooths message errors that vary sharply between neighbor variables, but corrects global errors across distant graph regions incrementally through long-range message propagations. We propose Hierarchy-GBP (H-GBP), an iterative, two-stage framework that accelerates GBP by first solving these global errors with a coarse graph approximation (abstraction) and projecting the results back to the original graph (recovery), then refining the remaining local errors with GBP. We prove H-GBP convergence to the optimum by deriving the combined matrix operator of our abstraction and recovery steps and analyzing its spectral radius. Experiments on linear sparse graphs show that H-GBP converges fundamentally faster than standard GBP. Moreover, we validate H-GBP on two important spatial problems: Pose Graph Optimization (PGO) and Bundle Adjustment (BA). H-GBP markedly accelerates large-scale PGO and achieves state-of-the-art runtime across all tested BA scales.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Hierarchy-GBP 两阶段迭代框架：先用粗化图的抽象求解全局误差、再投影回原图恢复，然后用 Gaussian Belief Propagation 细化局部误差，并从谱半径分析证明收敛。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「粗粒度状态抽象 + 恢复 + 局部精修」的层次化迭代结构可能与 LVR 中多尺度 latent 状态更新、误差跨距离传播及动态停止判定形成类比，可供核查。
